summary: Vellacombe delivery report (November 2005) to Corvenlea Pharma for programme VD-05-064: route scout for the CVL azaheterocycle series and delivery of 32 analogues. A revised heteroaryl coupling sequence replaced a difficult late-stage purification; compound cards with yields and LCMS purity are tabulated.
header: VD-05-064 | Corvenlea Pharma | Delivery report rev A

title_block.title: CVL azaheterocycle programme: route scout and first analogue delivery
title_block.subtitle: Chemistry report to Corvenlea Pharma
lines: Prepared by: Dr R. Calderwood, Head of Medicinal Chemistry

blocks.p: Corvenlea Pharma asked Vellacombe to establish a reliable route to the CVL aminopyrimidine amide analogue set and to deliver {{PRJ0008:n_compounds}} analogues for their kinase biology. The original route stalled at a late-stage heteroaryl coupling whose crude product needed two chromatographic purifications.

We moved the heteroaryl coupling earlier in the sequence and introduced the amide last. The revised route removed the problematic purification, and all {{PRJ0008:n_compounds}} analogues were delivered in three delivery lots between September and November 2005.
Hypothesis: the aminopyrimidine nitrogen was coordinating the catalyst in the late coupling, giving incomplete conversion and a close-running by-product.

list: Route A (original): amide formation, then heteroaryl coupling. Conversion stalled at 60-70%; by-product co-eluted.
Route B: heteroaryl coupling on the protected aminochloropyrimidine, then deprotection and amide formation. Clean conversion; simple crystallisation of the intermediate.
Route C: one-pot coupling and amidation. Abandoned after two runs; impurity profile worse than Route A.

blocks.p: Route gate (02/09/2005): Route B selected with Corvenlea Pharma's agreement. Route risk: the amine protecting group must be removed under mild acid, because stronger conditions degraded the heteroaryl coupling product in the scout.

Analogues were prepared in parallel from the common intermediate. Each compound card records isolated yield, identity (1H NMR and LC-MS) and HPLC purity (UV area % at 254 nm). Isolated yields are from the final step. The agreed release threshold was ≥90% HPLC purity; compounds below 95% are flagged on their cards.

list: Lot 1, 14/09/2005: first twelve analogues (interim chemistry note issued)
Lot 3, 07/11/2005: final ten analogues and this report

blocks.p: Solid samples were shipped at ambient temperature with compound cards. Retained samples (5 mg each) are held at Vellacombe for twelve months.

Route B is robust at 50-100 mg scale and suits further analogue work. All delivered material met the agreed ≥90% release threshold. Proposed next set: vary the amide aryl ring while holding the best heteroaryl groups from this delivery, once Corvenlea Pharma's biology data are available.
